name: Article Brief Deck
description: Turn an article or research packet into a clear, evidence-first presentation for teaching, curriculum planning, or editorial review. The deck keeps claims accurate while making the argument easy to scan and explain.
whatYouGet: A structured 16:9 HTML slide deck with an editorial modular-grid layout
Action titles that turn research findings into teachable decisions
Visible evidence cues, limitations, and source notes near each claim
Charts, comparisons, timelines, and cards selected for narrative clarity
A polished sample deck that can be adapted to a real article
goodFit: K-12 lesson explainers and curriculum planning meetings
Research-backed content briefs for education publishers
Client reviews where evidence and next actions must be explicit
notFor: Brand marketing decks or product sales presentations
Full academic papers or exhaustive literature reviews
Projects that depend on live web research or external fonts
requiredInputs: Article text, abstract, or research notes

faq.q: Can the deck simplify technical research?
faq.a: Yes. It can translate specialized findings into audience-appropriate language while preserving the original claim, evidence boundary, and important qualifications.
Yes. Source cues, dates, sample sizes, and limitations can appear beside the relevant statistic or claim so the evidence remains visible during presentation.

faq.q: Can it support a teaching workflow?
faq.a: Yes. The deck can connect the article to learner outcomes, discussion prompts, misconceptions, and practical next actions without pretending those ideas came from the source.

demoPrompt: /sl-article-brief-deck Create exactly 9 slides for Northfield Learning Lab on a fictional review of classroom retrieval practice. Move from claim and evidence to teaching moves, limits, and a three-week Grade 7 pilot. Title: “Retrieval practice can make science learning more durable”. Close: “Start with three minutes, measure what students can explain later”. Use concise action titles and a strict black, white, and red modular grid.
followUpPrompts: Adapt this deck for a parent-facing workshop while preserving the evidence qualifications.
Turn the research implications into a one-page teacher implementation brief.
Replace the fictional evidence with my article and flag every unsupported claim.
externalCostNote: No external services. Runs entirely on your agent.
